abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients with metastatic germ cell tumors undergo therapy including orchiectomy, chemotherapy and residual tumor resection. Even in case of metastatic disease, the treatment is still administered with curative intent. We present a case in which chemotherapy was successfully applied in an emergency setting prior to having histological confirmation of the suspected diagnosis of a germ cell tumor on our intensive care unit (ICU) while the patient was requiring mechanical ventilation, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) and vasopressor support. CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old man presented with massive testicular swelling, severe dyspnea, bilateral leg edema and acute postrenal kidney failure. A computed tomography (CT) scan revealed extensive pulmonary and retroperitoneal metastases and pneumonia. He was admitted to our intensive care unit with multiorgan dysfunction requiring mechanical ventilation, CRRT and vasopressor support. Laboratory findings revealed moderately elevated beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (570 mIU/ml) and an elevated lactate dehydrogenase over 2000 U/L. Due to his critical condition and high clinical suspicion of a metastatic germ cell tumor, chemotherapy according to the PEI regimen (cisplatin, etoposide, ifosfamide) was initiated only one day after the admission to our ICU before histological confirmation of the diagnosis. The patient showed marked clinical, laboratory and radiological improvement after one cycle. An orchiectomy later revealed necrotic tissue with residual seminoma. Subsequent cycles required dose reductions due to prolonged kidney failure, infectious complications during aplasia and cardiomyopathy leading to heart failure. Application of ifosfamide was discontinued after the patient suffered from severe ifosfamide-related toxicities, including Fanconi-syndrome and neurotoxicity. A Positron Emission Tomography-CT scan after four cycles demonstrated an overall regression of the tumor with residual lesions. CONCLUSION: Advanced testicular cancer can present as an acute emergency. In selected life-threatening situations, immediate chemotherapy is justified in patients with high clinical suspicion of a germ cell tumor, even in the absence of histological confirmation. The combination of clinical findings, the pattern of metastases, morphological findings in imaging and tumor markers should be used to define the most likely diagnosis beforehand.
abstract_ja: はじめに：転移性胚細胞腫瘍の患者は、精巣摘除術、化学療法、残存腫瘍の切除を含む治療を受ける。転移を有する場合でも、治療は根治を目指して行われる。本報告は、組織学的確定に先立ち、人工呼吸、持続的腎代替療法（CRRT）、昇圧薬を要するICUで、疑われる胚細胞腫瘍の診断に対して緊急化学療法を成功裏に行った症例である。症例提示：35歳男性が、巨大な精巣腫大、重度の呼吸困難、両下肢浮腫、急性の腎後性腎不全で来院した。CT検査で広範な肺および後腹膜転移と肺炎を認めた。多臓器不全に対して人工呼吸、CRRT、昇圧薬を要し、ICUに入室した。検査でβ-hCG（570 mIU/mL）の中等度上昇と乳酸脱水素酵素（LDH）2000 U/L超の上昇を認めた。重篤な状態と転移性胚細胞腫瘍の高い臨床的疑いから、ICU入室の1日後にPEI療法（シスプラチン、エトポシド、イホスファミド）を組織学的確定前に開始した。1コース後に臨床的、検査的、画像的に著明な改善を認めた。後の精巣摘除術で壊死組織と残存セミノーマが判明した。長期の腎機能障害、無顆粒球期の感染合併症、心筋症による心不全のため、後のコースでは用量減量を要した。イホスファミドは、ファンコニ症候群と神経毒性を含む重篤なイホスファミド関連毒性のため中止された。4コース後のPET-CTでは、残存病変を伴う全体的な腫瘍の縮小を認めた。結論：進行した精巣がんは急性の緊急事態として発症しうる。選択された生命を脅かす状況では、組織学的確定がなくても胚細胞腫瘍の臨床的疑いが高い患者に対して、直ちに化学療法を行うことが正当化される。臨床所見、転移のパターン、画像上の形態学的所見、腫瘍マーカーを組み合わせて、事前に最も可能性の高い診断を定めるべきである。
